NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: aim for 10..15% below maintenance calories.
    - Distribute calories evenly across 3 main meals and 1..2 snacks to support glycaemic control.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6..2.0g per kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40..45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25..30% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - Each meal to include lean protein, high-fibre vegetables, and a portion of low-GI carbohydrate.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined grains.
    - Include a source of healthy fat at each meal.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water daily.
  TIMING:
    - Avoid large carbohydrate loads at any single meal.
    - Pre-workout: small snack with protein and low-GI carb if needed (e.g. Greek yogurt + berries).
    - Post-workout: balanced meal with protein, low-GI carb, and vegetables.
  SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal and medication timing with exercise to reduce risk of hypoglycaemia.
    - Consult with a registered dietitian for individualized adjustments.

NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: aim for 10..15% below maintenance calories.
    - Distribute calories evenly across 3 main meals and 1..2 snacks to support glycaemic control.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6..2.0g per kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40..45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25..30% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - Each meal to include lean protein, high-fibre vegetables, and a portion of low-GI carbohydrate.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined grains.
    - Include a source of healthy fat at each meal.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water daily.
  TIMING:
    - Avoid large carbohydrate loads at any single meal.
    - Pre-workout: small snack with protein and low-GI carb if needed (e.g. Greek yogurt + berries).
    - Post-workout: balanced meal with protein, low-GI carb, and vegetables.
    - For fasted cardio: monitor blood glucose before and after, and do not perform if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L.
  SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal and medication timing with exercise to reduce risk of hypoglycaemia.
    - Consult with a registered dietitian for individualized adjustments.

NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: aim for 10..15% below maintenance calories.
    - Distribute calories evenly across 3 main meals and 1..2 snacks to support glycaemic control.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6..2.0g per kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40..45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25..30% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - Each meal to include lean protein, high-fibre vegetables, and a portion of low-GI carbohydrate.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined grains.
    - Include a source of healthy fat at each meal.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water daily.
  TIMING:
    - Avoid large carbohydrate loads at any single meal.
    - Pre-workout: small snack with protein and low-GI carb if needed (e.g. Greek yogurt + berries).
    - Post-workout: balanced meal with protein, low-GI carb, and vegetables.
    - For fasted cardio: monitor blood glucose before and after, and do not perform if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L.
  CHEAT_MEAL:
    - Allow one cheat meal per week, ideally at lunch.
    - Keep portion moderate and avoid excessive added sugars or deep-fried foods.
    - Monitor blood glucose 2 hours after cheat meal.
    - Resume regular eating pattern at next meal.
    - If possible, schedule cheat meal after a workout day to aid glucose handling.
  SPECIAL_CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal and medication timing with exercise to reduce risk of hypoglycaemia.
    - Consult with a registered dietitian for individualized adjustments.
  PRE_WORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO:
    - If blood glucose is above 5.5 mmol/L and she feels well, she may perform fasted cardio without breakfast.
    - If she prefers a light pre-workout meal or if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L, recommend:
      - 1 small apple or 1/2 banana (low-GI fruit)
      - 1 boiled egg or 100g Greek yogurt (protein)
      - Optional: 5–10 almonds (healthy fat)
    - Hydration: 250–500ml water before exercise.
    - Avoid high-sugar or high-fat foods pre-cardio.
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after session.
  POST_WORKOUT_SNACKS:
    - 100g Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup berries
    - 1 boiled egg + 1 small apple
    - 1 slice whole grain bread + 1 tbsp nut butter
    - 100g cottage cheese + 1/2 cup sliced cucumber
    - 1 small can tuna (in water) + 4–5 whole grain crackers
    - 1 protein shake (unsweetened, low-carb) + 1/2 banana
    - 1/2 cup hummus + carrot sticks
    - 1/2 cup edamame beans
    - Hydration: 250–500ml water post-exercise
    - All snacks are low-GI, include protein, and support glycaemic control
  INTERMITTENT_FASTING:
    - Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered with caution for type 2 diabetes, but only with medical supervision.
    - If she wishes to try IF, recommend a conservative approach such as 12:12 or 14:10 (fasting:eating window).
    - Avoid prolonged fasting (>16 hours) due to risk of hypoglycaemia, especially on metformin.
    - Maintain regular meal timing on training days, especially before and after workouts.
    - Do not perform fasted resistance training; fasted cardio is permitted only if morning glucose is >5.5 mmol/L and she feels well.
    - Monitor blood glucose closely during fasting periods and break the fast if symptoms of hypoglycaemia occur.
    - All meals during eating window should follow low-GI, high-fibre, moderate protein, and healthy fat guidelines.
    - Hydration: water, herbal tea, and black coffee (unsweetened) allowed during fasting window.
    - Consult with her physician and registered dietitian before starting IF or making changes to medication timing.

  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: aim for 10..15% below maintenance calories.
    - Distribute calories evenly across 3 main meals and 1..2 snacks to support glycaemic control.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6..2.0g per kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40..45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25..30% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - Each meal to include lean protein, high-fibre vegetables, and a portion of low-GI carbohydrate.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined grains.
    - Include a source of healthy fat at each meal.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water daily.
  TIMING:
    - Avoid large carbohydrate loads at any single meal.
    - Pre-workout: small snack with protein and low-GI carb if needed (e.g. Greek yogurt + berries).
    - Post-workout: balanced meal with protein, low-GI carb, and vegetables.
    - For fasted cardio: monitor blood glucose before and after, and do not perform if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L.
  CHEAT_MEAL:
    - Allow one cheat meal per week, ideally at lunch.
    - Keep portion moderate and avoid excessive added sugars or deep-fried foods.
    - Monitor blood glucose 2 hours after cheat meal.
    - Resume regular eating pattern at next meal.
    - If possible, schedule cheat meal after a workout day to aid glucose handling.
  SPECIAL_CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal and medication timing with exercise to reduce risk of hypoglycaemia.
    - Consult with a registered dietitian for individualized adjustments.
  PRE_WORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO:
    - If blood glucose is above 5.5 mmol/L and she feels well, she may perform fasted cardio without breakfast.
    - If she prefers a light pre-workout meal or if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L, recommend:
      - 1 small apple or 1/2 banana (low-GI fruit)
      - 1 boiled egg or 100g Greek yogurt (protein)
      - Optional: 5–10 almonds (healthy fat)
    - Hydration: 250–500ml water before exercise.
    - Avoid high-sugar or high-fat foods pre-cardio.
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after session.
  POST_WORKOUT_SNACKS:
    - 100g Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup berries
    - 1 boiled egg + 1 small apple
    - 1 slice whole grain bread + 1 tbsp nut butter
    - 100g cottage cheese + 1/2 cup sliced cucumber
    - 1 small can tuna (in water) + 4–5 whole grain crackers
    - 1 protein shake (unsweetened, low-carb) + 1/2 banana
    - 1/2 cup hummus + carrot sticks
    - 1/2 cup edamame beans
    - Hydration: 250–500ml water post-exercise
    - All snacks are low-GI, include protein, and support glycaemic control

NUTRITION
  ENERGY:
    - Moderate calorie deficit: aim for 10..15% below maintenance calories.
    - Distribute calories evenly across 3 main meals and 1..2 snacks to support glycaemic control.
  MACROS:
    - Protein: 1.6..2.0g per kg bodyweight per day.
    - Carbohydrate: 40..45% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables).
    - Fat: 25..30% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds).
  MEAL STRUCTURE:
    - Each meal to include lean protein, high-fibre vegetables, and a portion of low-GI carbohydrate.
    - Avoid added sugars and minimize refined grains.
    - Include a source of healthy fat at each meal.
    - Hydration: at least 2L water daily.
  TIMING:
    - Avoid large carbohydrate loads at any single meal.
    - Pre-workout: small snack with protein and low-GI carb if needed (e.g. Greek yogurt + berries).
    - Post-workout: balanced meal with protein, low-GI carb, and vegetables.
    - For fasted cardio: monitor blood glucose before and after, and do not perform if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L.
  CHEAT_MEAL:
    - Allow one cheat meal per week, ideally at lunch.
    - Keep portion moderate and avoid excessive added sugars or deep-fried foods.
    - Monitor blood glucose 2 hours after cheat meal.
    - Resume regular eating pattern at next meal.
    - If possible, schedule cheat meal after a workout day to aid glucose handling.
  SPECIAL_CONSIDERATIONS:
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after exercise, especially when increasing intensity or duration.
    - Carry a fast-acting carbohydrate (e.g. glucose tablets) in case of hypoglycaemia.
    - Coordinate meal and medication timing with exercise to reduce risk of hypoglycaemia.
    - Consult with a registered dietitian for individualized adjustments.
  PRE_WORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO:
    - If blood glucose is above 5.5 mmol/L and she feels well, she may perform fasted cardio without breakfast.
    - If she prefers a light pre-workout meal or if morning glucose is <5.5 mmol/L, recommend:
      - 1 small apple or 1/2 banana (low-GI fruit)
      - 1 boiled egg or 100g Greek yogurt (protein)
      - Optional: 5–10 almonds (healthy fat)
    - Hydration: 250–500ml water before exercise.
    - Avoid high-sugar or high-fat foods pre-cardio.
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after session.
  POST_WORKOUT_SNACKS:
    - 100g Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup berries
    - 1 boiled egg + 1 small apple
    - 1 slice whole grain bread + 1 tbsp nut butter
    - 100g cottage cheese + 1/2 cup sliced cucumber
    - 1 small can tuna (in water) + 4–5 whole grain crackers
    - 1 protein shake (unsweetened, low-carb) + 1/2 banana
    - 1/2 cup hummus + carrot sticks
    - 1/2 cup edamame beans
    - Hydration: 250–500ml water post-exercise
    - All snacks are low-GI, include protein, and support glycaemic control
  INTERMITTENT_FASTING:
    - Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered with caution for type 2 diabetes, but only with medical supervision.
    - If she wishes to try IF, recommend a conservative approach such as 12:12 or 14:10 (fasting:eating window).
    - Avoid prolonged fasting (>16 hours) due to risk of hypoglycaemia, especially on metformin.
    - Maintain regular meal timing on training days, especially before and after workouts.
    - Do not perform fasted resistance training; fasted cardio is permitted only if morning glucose is >5.5 mmol/L and she feels well.
    - Monitor blood glucose closely during fasting periods and break the fast if symptoms of hypoglycaemia occur.
    - All meals during eating window should follow low-GI, high-fibre, moderate protein, and healthy fat guidelines.
    - Hydration: water, herbal tea, and black coffee (unsweetened) allowed during fasting window.
    - Consult with her physician and registered dietitian before starting IF or making changes to medication timing.
